name: maybe_Ui_ListCursor_IsAtPartyCountSlot
summary: True when the list cursor is on the first extra slot after the active party rows. Used by the equipment window to decide which of its two panes owns the highlighted row.
evidence: asm 0x63B5E4: idx=func_0063A794(self) (reads self->f_38->f_c, the row-list cursor), n=func_0063A8A0(self+0x410); return idx==n. 0x63A8A0 ignores its argument and returns 0x643504(gameState), which counts the party members in gameState->f_27218 whose per-character flag byte (state + charId*g_00643580*4 + 0xcc) has bit0 set (= in party). Callers Ui_EquipmentWindow_Confirm/Update/FndItemIndex choose between panes f_5f4 and f_654 based on this test plus 0x63B60C/0x63B638.

name: maybe_Ui_ListCursor_IsAtPartyCountSlotPlus1
summary: True when the list cursor is one row past the active party count (second extra slot of the equipment list).
evidence: Same two helpers as 0x63B5E4 but the comparison in the assembly is idx == n+1 (`cmp r5,r0` after `add r0,r0,#1`). Part of the three-way pane pick used by Ui_EquipmentWindow_* (callers 0x1993C4, 0x1994F4, 0x199E30, 0x19B950).

name: maybe_Ui_ListCursor_IsPastPartyCountSlots
summary: True when the list cursor is two or more rows past the active party count.
evidence: asm 0x63B638: `add r0,r0,#2; cmp r5,r0; movge r0,#1` i.e. return (partyCount+2 <= cursor). Third member of the pane-selection triple used by Ui_EquipmentWindow_Update/Confirm.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_IsTransitionBusy_State4A8
summary: Reports that a screen transition is still running while this window is in its f_4a8 mode; used to hold back input/animation.

Ui_GetCore->f_14 is the fade/transition manager (Ui_IsEndFade 0x1659EC uses core->f_14+0x10/+0x1c with vtable+0x34 as its IsEnd). Caller 0x295790. No body for vtable slots, so the exact 'busy' wording is inferred from the neighbouring transition helpers.

name: maybe_Ui_ModelSelect_IsShowing

name: maybe_Ui_ListWidget_GetCellValueWithDefault
summary: Returns the value of the highlighted list cell (a u16 from the cell array) or one of the two fallback constants when the cursor is on an empty/placeholder cell.
evidence: 0x640FC4: n = self->vtable[0x64](self); row = self[0x16]; if the row exists and self[0xe] (the row pointer at +0x38) is neither null nor type 0x13, return *(u16*)(self[0x16] + ((row->f_c + self[0x14]*8) - n)*2); the attrs return g_00641048 (no row) or g_0064104C (type 0x13 = separator/heading). The same field layout appears in every list helper in this file. Callers Ui_SkillPanel_HandleInput, 0x36F2E0, 0x3AC338.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_IsTransitionBusy_State12
summary: Same transition-busy test as 0x63BEFC but only for windows whose state byte f_578 equals 0x12.
evidence: 0x6410F4: if (self->f_578 == 0x12) { core=Ui_GetCore(&s); if (core->f_14->f_c->vtable[0x18]()) return 1; } return 0. Sibling 0x641574 does the same for state 0x13; both are vtable-only (no direct callers).

name: maybe_Ui_Entry_GetIconId
summary: Maps an entry reference to the icon id used to draw it, returning -1 when the reference is empty or has no icon in the loaded icon bank.

The exact icon-vs-glyph semantics are inferred from the 8-byte bank records and the -1 sentinel.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_IsTransitionBusy

name: maybe_Ui_Window_SetStateMessageArgs

name: Item_CountEquipped
signature: int Item_CountEquipped(const GameState* state, int charId, int itemId, int matchByKind)
summary: Counts how many party members have the given item equipped. charId 0xff walks the whole party; matchByKind compares item categories instead of exact ids; a two-handed weapon consumes both hand slots.
evidence: 0x642F54 walks gameState->f_27218 party entries (via 0x66B0E4) and their 6 equipment slots at +0xEC/+0x11C. Item ids 0xa4..(0xa4+g_0064331C) and 0xb19..0xb1c are treated as equipment; 0x61BD4C resolves an item id to its record. When slot index == 1 and 0x66C5CC(item) is true the loop skips a slot, i.e. a two-handed weapon. Callers 0x6301A4/0x6302EC compare it against 0x643324 (owned count) to decide whether an equipped item may be sold.

name: Ui_ListWidget_GetSelectedItemId
summary: Returns the item id stored in the highlighted cell of a list widget (rows of six columns, 0x118-byte entries, value in the low half-word at +0x50).
evidence: 0x64448C: index = (self->f_38->f_c + self[0x13]*6 - self->vtable[0x68]()); return *(short*)((int*)self + index*0x46 + 0x14) (stride 0x46 ints = 0x118 bytes, offset 0x14 ints = 0x50). Caller 0x1BFC50 feeds the result straight into item lookups (0x61BD4C, 0x311134) and stores it as an item id; poker/casino windows use the same widget.

name: maybe_Ui_IsWindowReady
summary: True when no message window is open, or when the open window has both of its readiness flags (f_3d/f_3e) set; a general 'the UI is idle, safe to continue' test.
evidence: 0x645A6C: w = Ui_GetCore(&s)->f_10->f_98 (the current message/window object); return !w || (w->f_3d != 0 && w->f_3e != 0). The same window object and flags are used by the message-window code (0x1993C4 checks core->f_10->f_98 the same way). No callers (vtable slot).

name: Ui_BagCategory_CountItems
summary: Counts the entries of a bag category (stride-0x1c entry array) that pass the visibility filter and the category/flag test; drives the 'x items' counters of the bag's category rows.
evidence: 0x6462C4 iterates list->f_4 .. list->f_4 + list->f_8*0x1c and counts entries where 0x64733C(list, entry) != 0 and 0x3AA574(list->f_0, entry->u16@8, category) != 0. Called from maybe_Ui_SixRowCountList_Populate (0x45309C) which fills 6 category rows (name, count, ...) for the bag screen.

name: Gfx_Sprite_SetFrameUVFromRecord
signature: void Gfx_Sprite_SetFrameUVFromRecord(SpriteAtlas* self, GfxSprite* sprite, u32 frameId)
summary: Sets a sprite's texture UV rectangle from an atlas/icon record looked up by frame id; hides the sprite when the record is missing.
evidence: 0x6464D4: if (self->f_8c == 0) return; rec = 0x64609C(self, frameId); if (!rec) { sprite->f_44 &= ~1; return; } uv0=(rec->f_c, rec->f_e), uv1=(u16@8, u16@a); Gfx_Sprite_SetFrameUV(sprite, *self->f_8c->f_90->f_24, &uv0, &uv1). The record also carries a 0xRRGGBBAA colour at f_10 (see 0x646400). Callers: none (vtable slot).

name: Gfx_Sprite_SetFrameUVFromPackedRecord
signature: void Gfx_Sprite_SetFrameUVFromPackedRecord(SpriteAtlas* self, GfxSprite* sprite, u32 frameId)
summary: Same as 0x6464D4 but for atlas records whose four UV coordinates are stored as consecutive u16 fields at +0..+6.
evidence: 0x646588 is byte-identical to 0x6464D4 except that the record is read as u16[0..3] (puVar1[0..3]) instead of f_c/f_e/u16@8/u16@a, i.e. two packing variants of the same icon record. Callers: none (vtable slot).

name: Ui_Entry_GetDisplayText
summary: Resolves the display string for a UI entry id: plain item/skill entries go through the message table, monster entries set message argument 5 and return their inline name, unknown ids return the 'no data' string.
evidence: 0x646728 bounds entryId by g_00646A1C, looks the record up with 0x63CF74, then switches on the record type byte: type 0 -> 0x45A1E0 + 0x18C184 + 0x63D790(record->f_2b2) returns a message string; type 1 -> 0x18C1B8 + 0x628FFC; type 2 -> 0x63EB4C(u16@4), Message_SetArg(5,...) and the inline string at record+4. Returns g_00646A20 for out-of-range and u_no_data_00646A50 for empty records. Caller maybe_Ui_PlateWidget_Draw (0x228CA0).

name: maybe_Ui_BagCategory_FilterAvailable
signature: void maybe_Ui_BagCategory_FilterAvailable(u32* out, BagListOwner* owner, int category)
summary: Keeps only those of the seven bag-category bytes that actually have at least one matching item, packing the surviving categories into the 7-byte result.
evidence: 0x646BB4 first builds the candidate category list with 0x646C4C (up to 7 category bytes taken from the per-category records' f_19), then for each byte calls 0x3AA574(owner->f_0, category, byte) and copies the byte to the output. 0x3AA574 is the 'item belongs to category/flag' test also used by Ui_BagCategory_CountItems. Called from maybe_Ui_PlateWidget_Draw and maybe_Ui_ItemRows_UpdateIcons.

name: Gfx_Sprite_SetFrameUVFromBank
signature: void Gfx_Sprite_SetFrameUVFromBank(SpriteAtlas* self, GfxSprite* sprite, int frameIndex, int unused)
summary: Applies a texture and UV rectangle to a sprite from a texture bank indexed by frame number, hiding the sprite when the index is outside the bank.
evidence: 0x647238 first calls 0x64715C(sprite, self->f_4c) to bind the texture, then takes sprite[0x25]/[0x24] (the bound texture object), checks 0 <= frameIndex <= texture->f_60 and reads the 0x10-byte frame record at texture->f_58->f_24 + frameIndex*0x10 (u16@8, u16@a, f_c, f_e) before Gfx_Sprite_SetFrameUV. On failure it clears sprite->f_44 bit0 so the sprite is not drawn. Callers: none (vtable slot).

name: maybe_Ui_ListWidget_GetCursorValue
summary: Looks up the value of the list element under the current global cursor index, returning g_0064854C when the index is out of range or the element is missing.
evidence: 0x6484EC: i = 0x64E928() (the shared cursor index also read by Ui_RecordWindow_Update/HandleInput); n = self->vtable[8](self) (count); if (i < n && self->vtable[0x10](self,i)) return self[i+2] >> 16; else return g_0064854C. Used by the monster book / record window (callers 0x243C84, maybe_Ui_MonsterBook_DrawModel, maybe_Ui_MonsterBook_HandleInput). The upper-half-word expression is Ghidra's view of the element payload, so the exact field is not verified.

name: maybe_Ui_Text_Preload
summary: Ensures the shared 0x98-byte UI core object exists and resolves a text id through it; the returned string is discarded here, so the only visible effect is the lazy initialisation.
evidence: 0x648A80 is the same lazy-singleton pattern as 0x6F229C/0x6F2394 (flag byte, 0x11FE8C align, 0x11CFAC div, 0x116AE0 clear, 0x627308 alloc, vtable g_00648B2C) and then calls 0x633560(core->f_10, textId). 0x633560 is the UI text-id lookup (many callers pass ui_text.bxon ids such as 0xd 'どうぐぶくろ', 0xbd 'だいじなもの'; ids resolved with the extracted table). No callers, so this is probably a vtable slot or dead code.

name: Ui_ListCursor_GetClampedRow
summary: Returns the party-relative row selected by the list cursor, or 0x1f when the cursor is outside the active party rows. Used by the strength/status window.
evidence: 0x648BFC: if (func_0063A794(self) < func_0063A8A0(self+0x410)) return func_0063A7D8(self+0x410, cursor); else 0x1f. 0x63A7D8 maps a row index to the party member's byte at record+200 (0xff when out of range), 0x63A8A0 is the party count, 0x1f is the 'no selection' sentinel used throughout this UI. Callers: Ui_TsuyosaWindow_InitPanes/Update/UpdateSelection/OnInput.

name: Ui_SmithMenu_GetCellIndex
summary: Converts the smith menu's row counter into the flat cell index of its five-column list, wrapping with &0xff.
evidence: 0x64D59C: (rowFromCursor + self->f_13*5 - self->vtable[0x68]()) & 0xff. f_13 is the row field also used by 0x6551C0 (same formula with stride 6), vtable+0x68 returns the number of visible columns. Callers: maybe_Ui_SmithMenu_UpdateCategory/UpdateDetailList/OpenPage.

name: maybe_Ui_BagList_SetLabel
signature: void maybe_Ui_BagList_SetLabel(UiBagList* self, int row, u32 unused, u32 arg4)
summary: Shows the selected row of a bag list, or - when the row is out of range - the bag-name label 0xd (tool bag) / 0xe (equipment bag) depending on the list's f_5 flag.
evidence: 0x64DF88: if (row < func_0063A8A0()) { func_0063A87C(self,row,...); return; } else pick text id 0xd or 0xe from self->f_5 and emit it with 0x633560(core->f_10, id); ids 0xd='どうぐぶくろ' and 0xe='そうびぶくろ' in the extracted ui_text table. Sibling 0x64DFF0 returns the row count plus that same flag.

name: Ui_EquipmentList_GetClampedRow
summary: Equipment-window twin of 0x648BFC: returns the selected party row, or 0x1f when the cursor points past the active party.
evidence: 0x64E010 has the same shape as 0x648BFC (0x63A8A0 party count, 0x63A794 cursor, 0x63A7D8 row->member lookup, 0x1f sentinel) but reads the cursor and count from the other panel object. Callers Ui_EquipmentWindow_UseItemLogic/SelectItem/0x19B950.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpritePane_SetTransform
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SpritePane_SetTransform(SpritePaneNode* self, u8* paneArray, int paneIndex, int isPrimary)
summary: Copies the transform of two sub-panes from the shared 0x9c-byte pane array into the front or back transform set of a two-pane sprite node, and toggles its visibility bit.
evidence: 0x654E34 indexes arg2 + paneIndex*0x9c, sets self->f_88->f_44 bit0 = (arg4 && arg3==5), then either copies +0x70/+0xa4 and pushes +0xd8/+0xec (isPrimary==0) or copies +0x688/+0x6bc/+0x6f0 (isPrimary!=0) via 0x654EF0. Callers 0x4C2DF0 and friends flush a 2D node's pending state and call the 0x53E220/0x53E9A4 (PICA) helpers, so this is sprite/pane placement rather than game logic.

name: maybe_Ui_SmithMenu_GetMaterialCellValue
summary: Returns the material id of the smith menu's selected cell, or the 'none' sentinel g_00655214 when the cell index is outside the material array.
evidence: 0x6551C0: idx = (cursor + self[0x13]*6 - self->vtable[0x68]()); if (idx < (self[0x15]-self[0x14])>>1) return *(u16*)(self[0x14] + idx*2); else g_00655214. Callers are the smith (alchemy) menu handlers 0x3EEB2C/0x3EEC70/0x3EEDA8.

name: Gfx_Texture_Upload
signature: void Gfx_Texture_Upload(TextureDesc* tex, CmdList* cmd, u32 stages, int needSync)
summary: Uploads one texture level to the GPU: converts the source pixels to the PICA200 layout for the texture format (RGBA8 / RGB8 / RGBA4 / RGB565 / RGBA5551), computes the level size and emits the fill/copy commands.
evidence: 0x656080 switches on tex->f_4 (byte at +4) for formats 0..4, builds the packed colour/format word from tex->f_4..f_7 (float 0..1 clamped by g_00656394/g_00656398/g_006563A0), multiplies width*height by 4/2/3 bytes per pixel and finally calls 0x6BA234 (optional sync) and 0x6B9E08 -> 0x6BE724, which writes a type-2 copy descriptor with 0x10/0x18/0x20 bpp into the 0x1c-byte command ring. Caller: Gfx (vtable only).

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_SetNodePosFromArgs
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Scene_SetNodePosFromArgs(SceneActor* self, u32* scene, u32 actorIndex, int nodeIndex, u32 valueSource)
summary: Writes a fixed-point position into one node of a 0x278-byte-by-0x2c-node scene record, using the float readers 0x5080D0/0x508AF8 for the coordinates.
evidence: 0x65BE30: base = *scene + (actorIndex & 0xffff)*0x278 + 4; node = base + nodeIndex*0x2c; two 0x5080D0()/0x508AF8() reads are packed as (low | high<<16) into node->f_14 and the third into node->f_18, plus a flag. self->f_28 == 9 / 0xb select the alternative field layout. Caller 0x55EBC0 (a scene setup routine that fills the same 0x278 records).

name: Container_HashMap_FindByKey
signature: void* Container_HashMap_FindByKey(u32* key, u32 keyLen, u32 unused, u32 seed)
summary: Looks an object up in the global hash map by a 0x40-byte key: hashes the first word, walks the bucket's intrusive list and compares the stored 16-word key with memcmp.
evidence: 0x6647CC reads the global map header (g_006648B0 bucket mask, g_006648B4 table, g_006648BC seed), masks (key>>0xc), walks the list at entry+0x7c and compares 0x40 bytes with 0x123660 (memcmp). 0x7135D4/0x7139AC are byte-identical variants over different registries. Callers maybe_Ui_EntryList_FindByIdList/FindByKeyList.

name: maybe_Party_FindEntryById
summary: Linear search of the party/actor table (up to 50 records of 0x8c bytes) for the record whose id at +0x88 equals *idPtr, skipping empty or over-long names.
evidence: asm 0x66AE3C: base = arg1 + 0x5FE4, stride = 0x8C (7*r*4), count limit 0x32; a record is skipped when strlen16(record) >= 7, when its first u16 is 0, or when its +0x88 dword is -1. Returns the record pointer or 0. The 0x8c record stride and the 0x24A98/f_27218 party table are the same ones used by Item_CountEquipped. Caller 0x2D5F54 (screen list builder) and 0x66AF34.

name: maybe_Party_EntryMatchesSelectedId
summary: True when the party-table entry found for *idPtr carries the same id that the current selection table holds for this list.
evidence: asm 0x66AF34: p = maybe_Party_FindEntryById(list, *idPtr); return p && (*(int*)(0x8740 + list) != -1) && (p->f_88 != -1) && (*(int*)(0x8740 + list) == p->f_88). The 0x8740 base is the literal g_0066AF80; Ghidra indexes it with the list pointer, which looks like a per-list selection table. Caller 0x2D5F54.

name: maybe_Text_MeasureNameRef
summary: Measures the rendered width of a name reference: takes the string buffer for the current text renderer, searches it for the terminator over the fixed-point length, and returns the base advance minus the character width.
evidence: 0x66C470 takes w = *(u8*)(ref->f_4 + 0x14) (fixed-point character width), buf = 0x51B1FC(renderer+0x98, 0x7fffffff), n = 0x11CD80(buf, w*2+1) (a memchr-style scan) and returns *(u16*)(ref->f_4+0x12) + (n - w). Same caller family as Text_FormatMessageArg (the 0x6E33xx status rows), i.e. two-column text layout arithmetic. The inner helpers 0x51B1FC/0x11CD80 have no decompiled body, so their exact contract is inferred.

name: Text_FormatMessageArg
summary: Formats a message argument / name reference into a static wide buffer, optionally stripping CR/LF, and prefixes the value with the unit or label selected by the reference type.
evidence: 0x66C99C resolves the string via 0x63CDD8(table, id - typeByte), copies it into g_0066CCA4 while dropping 0x0d/0x0a when arg2 != 0, then switches on the type byte at ref->f_8+0x10: 1/2/3 format with text ids 0x24/0x25/0x26 (the unit glyphs ㍉/㌔/㌢ in ui_text.bxon) using 0x707CAC (snprintf) into g_0066CC98. 58 callers including Text_ProcessControlTag, Ui_MessageWindow_ShowNextPage and Ui_CharaStatusWindow_FillPartyMember, all feeding Message_SetArg -> this is the generic 'message argument to display string' helper.

name: maybe_Gfx_Node_InitInlineListA
summary: Initialises a node that owns a large inline sub-object at +0xe0f8, then destroys the temporary returned by that sub-object's constructor and returns the node.
evidence: asm 0x66D680: store {owner, owner+0x18} at self; call 0x5761D8(self+0xE0F8) (a constructor that installs the vtable 0x00782668 and releases a resource via svc 0x23); subtract 0xE0F8-4/-0xF4 from the result and tail-call 0x10F6CC, which is the deleting-destructor trampoline (loads the vtable at object-8 and calls slot +4). Byte-identical duplicate at 0x66D928. No callers (vtable slot).

name: Monster_AttachAnimation
summary: Loads the enemy animation for the given id and binds it to this monster model's node at +0x60.
evidence: 0x66D808 calls the virtual slot +0x20 of the object at self-4, resolves the target with maybe_Os_FindObjectByHandle(self+8), then Monster_LoadEnemyAnimation(animationId, self->f_c, ...) and 0x576CDC(anim, handle+0x60, &local). Callers: none (vtable slot); the adjacent names Monster_LoadEnemyAnimation/Os_FindObjectByHandle come from other batches' outputs.

name: maybe_Gfx_Node_InitInlineListB
summary: Second copy of 0x66D680 (identical machine code) for a node class that is not otherwise distinguished; initialises the inline sub-object at +0xe0f8 and returns the node.
evidence: asm 0x66D928 is byte-for-byte identical to 0x66D680 (same constants 0xE0F8, 0x5761D8, 0x10F6CC), so the two classes share their layout; neither has callers (vtable slots). Kept as a separate name because they are separate entry points in the retail image.

name: maybe_Gfx_RenderCallback_Dispatch
summary: Calls the global render-callback installed in the graphics module, twice for nodes that own a child object (once with no arguments for the child, once with the node).
evidence: 0x6B8FB8 loads g_006B8FF4 and, when slot +4 is non-null and the argument is non-null, calls it once if node->f_4 != 0 and then jumps to it with the node. Ghidra cannot recover the jump table ('too many branches'), so the exact overload set is unknown. Callers 0x4FD6B0/0x500900.

name: Gfx_GpuCmd_CaptureScreen
signature: void Gfx_GpuCmd_CaptureScreen(CmdList* cmd, u32 srcLeft, u32 srcTop, u32 srcRight, u32 srcBottom, u32 dest, u32 width, u32 height, u32 format, u32 screen, u32 flags, u32 bpp)
summary: Emits a display-transfer (framebuffer capture) command: 0x500/0x501/0x502 select top screen, bottom screen or both, 0x10/0x18/0x20 select the pixel size.
evidence: 0x6B9D3C is a thin wrapper over 0x6BE47C, which maps arg10 0x500/0x501/0x502 to 1/2/both-screen transfers and arg5 0x8051/0x8056/... to the source format, then writes a command descriptor into the 0x1c-byte ring at cmd->f_18 + cmd->f_20*0x1c. Caller 0x563244 passes 400/0xf0 (screen sizes) and 0x500, i.e. a screen grab.

name: Gfx_GpuCmd_CopyTexture
signature: void Gfx_GpuCmd_CopyTexture(CmdList* cmd, u32 src, u32 dest, u32 size, int bpp, u32 srcStride, u32 destStride, u32 height, int heightBpp)
summary: Emits a type-2 GPU copy descriptor (source address, destination address, size and stride, with the texture height encoded in the top bits for 16/24/32-bit formats).
evidence: 0x6B9E08 wraps 0x6BE724, which writes a descriptor at cmd->f_18 + cmd->f_20*0x1c with *entry = 2, +4 = src, +8 = size, and packs (height & 0x7fffff) into the stride words, setting bits 0x800000/0x1000000 for 0x18/0x20-bpp. Called from Gfx_Texture_Upload (0x656080).

name: Gfx_GpuCmd_Fill
summary: Emits a memory-fill GPU command (six parameter words incl. the 0x12345678 fill constant and its mask) and patches the previous descriptor when the command list grew across a boundary.
evidence: 0x6B9F2C and its twin 0x6BA234 write [1, 0x000F0111, 1, 0x000F0111, 0x12345678, mask] into the ring at cmd->f_18 + cmd->f_20*0x1c, set the entry's type bits (|4 or |5 depending on cmd->f_3d) and bump cmd->f_20. 0x6B9F2C additionally repairs the previous entry through 0x1160AC when cmd->f_34 is set. Callers: maybe_Gfx_Overlay_BeginDraw/DrawContent and 0x563244. The GPU register id 0x000F0111 is not decoded here, so 'fill' is inferred from the constant-value/mask pair.

evidence: 0x006E3904 pushes a row with Ui_Window_PushPane/0x6D7508(host+0x120, 0, <textId,flags from the row table 0x729A7C+0x28>, 0), sets slots 3/4 with 0x617D7C(self,3,0)/(self,4,0) for the unknown case, and for a known value does Message_SetArg(6, 0x633560(uiCore->f_10, 0x3d), 0): the asm shows `mov r1,#0x3d; ldr r0,[r0,#0x10]; bl 0x633560`, and that id is the ui_text.bxon entry 'きようさ (deftness)' in game_assets/tables/packs/gamecmn/ui_text.json. It then adds the measured width (0x66C470) to a per-row accumulator (column field f_1ce), re-lays-out the entry (0x19201C) and registers it in the compendium (0x618394). All ten functions are byte-identical apart from the label id and that accumulator field (diff 0x6E3364 vs 0x6E3544/0x6E3904 changes only those), so they are the ten labelled stat rows of the status screen; the literal pool also carries the 999 threshold used to switch to the four-digit layout. The hosting window is inferred from the label set, not from a caller (these are vtable slots).

name: maybe_Ui_ScrollList_WrapCursorA
signature: void maybe_Ui_ScrollList_WrapCursorA(UiListWidget* self, int delta, u32 unused, int pageCount)
summary: Moves the list's scroll/cursor offset by delta and wraps it into range using the widget's item count and a fixed fraction; used by the tactics window and the scroll bar.
evidence: 0x6E51E4: self[0x13] += delta; n = self->vtable[0x64](self); half = (g_006E53A0 * (n-1)) >> 32; if (self[0x13] < 0) self[0x13] = (half>>2) - (half>>31). The second half of the function is truncated by Ghidra ('bad instruction'), so the upper clamp is not visible. Callers Ui_SakusenWindow_Confirm, maybe_Ui_ScrollBar_Update.

signature: void maybe_Ui_ScrollList_WrapCursorB(UiListWidget* self, int delta, u32 unused, int pageCount)

name: maybe_Ui_ScrollList_MoveCursorWithPage
signature: void maybe_Ui_ScrollList_MoveCursorWithPage(UiListWidget* self, int delta, u32 unused, int pageCount)

name: Pack_AcquireResourceHandle
signature: int Pack_AcquireResourceHandle(PackHandle* out, PackEntry* entry, u32 unused, u32 arg4)
summary: Validates a pack entry (type id g_006F1068, at least 0x28 bytes of data, part binder 0x570D1C) and stores it as the new handle in out[0]/out[1], releasing the previous handle.
evidence: 0x6F0F5C walks the entry list comparing the type id with g_006F1068, requires entry[0x16] != 0 and entry[0x17] >= 0x28, calls 0x570D1C, then 0x124F60/0x124D48 to take the handle and 0x1241D0/0x124DD0 to drop the handles previously stored in out[1]. Callers 0x4B9590/0x4BA3F0/0x4BB154.

name: Pack_ReleaseResourceHandle
summary: Releases the pack handle stored in handle[1] (hash-table based release) and clears the cached pointer and tag.
evidence: 0x6F1074: *handle = 0; if the tag at handle[1] is present in the global handle table (g_006F10D0 mask / g_006F10D4 table) call 0x1241D0 to free the entry, then stamp handle[1] with the empty tag g_006F10D8. Callers 0x4B9590/0x4BB154, i.e. the same resource owner as 0x6F0F5C.

name: Ui_GetCore

name: Container_Vector_PushBack
summary: Appends a zeroed 12-byte element to an intrusive vector and returns a pointer to it, growing the backing array through ldiv/size maths and 0x563540 when full.

Callers are the model-variant/loader paths 0x30AFF4/0x30B120/0x30B5F4/0x30B628.

name: maybe_Container_HashMap_FindByNameA
summary: Registry lookup: hashes a 0x40-byte key, walks one of the global hash buckets and returns the registered object of type g_00713710 whose key matches.

Caller Ui_WorldMap_LoadModels (0x17E2F0), so this registry holds world-map model resources.

name: maybe_Ui_Layout_BindPartA
signature: void maybe_Ui_Layout_BindPartA(u8* screenType, int* out, u32 nameHash)
